message: The engine's review and audit personas (the files under .claude/agents/) each declare a role, a model-tier, an optional lens, and a write posture (permissions), and those declarations must hold together. The load-bearing case is a read-only persona: a reviewer or the audit persona declared read-only must actually be one the platform blocks from editing the work it reviews — it must block the authoritative-write tools (Edit, Write, NotebookEdit) via disallowedTools or a write-excluding tools allowlist, never inherit every tool. This check parses each persona's frontmatter and runs the agent coherence leg over it, going red when a role/model-tier is outside its closed set, a lens sits on a role that carries none, or a read-only persona does not block the write tools (most importantly when it declares no tool lock at all and silently inherits write access) — so a regression is caught at merge rather than shipping a read-only reviewer that can change the work. A second leg guards git safety: a persona the platform would let run the Bash shell must carry the git-safety recipe in its own text (work only in a throwaway copy you make yourself with engine_fixture.clone_engine(); never git worktree add from an existing checkout, never repoint a remote, never stash or reset a checkout you did not create), so a review agent following the shipped pack cannot mutate a shared checkout's real git state and the recipe travels in the pack rather than living in session memory. These legs enforce that the write-tool lock and the git-safety recipe are DECLARED; they do not police what a shell does at runtime or writes through any write-capable MCP tools the session exposes — confining those is the build's worktree isolation plus the protected-branch merge gate, not this check. To fix: correct the flagged persona in .claude/agents/<name>.md — a read-only persona carries disallowedTools blocking Edit/Write/NotebookEdit, and a shell-capable persona states the git-safety recipe in its body.
